Elena V.: Heads-up: opened a small docs PR focused on backpressure + sync->async migration snippets for SDK examples across Py/TS/Go. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4499
Noah R.: Nice. What's the main change?
Elena V.: 1) Python: show converting sync generator examples to async iterator + how to apply backoff when stream stalls; 2) TS: add a tiny browser vs node note for streaming reader usage; 3) Go: clarify grpc vs http stream handling and show ctx cancel + retry; 4) add an explicit note about token accounting for partial flushes.
Chen L.: Can you paste the Python migration snippet? I want to ensure the async semantics are correct.
Elena V.: Sure:
```python
# sync generator -> async iterator shim
async def async_from_sync(sync_gen):
    for item in sync_gen:
        yield item

# usage
async for chunk in async_from_sync(client.stream_sync(req)):
    process(chunk)
```
Noah R.: Tiny nit: the shim above is sync; for large workloads we should run the sync generator in a threadpool to avoid blocking the event loop. Maybe show `loop.run_in_executor`.
Elena V.: Good catch. Updated to show run_in_executor variant with a one-line note.
Ada M.: For TS I added both `ReadableStream` reader example and a `for await (const chunk of stream)` wrapper for node-compatible runtimes. Also noted that some runtimes require base64 decode for resume tokens and showed `Buffer.from(...,'base64').toString()` + `atob` variants.
Chen L.: Go example?
Elena V.: Go shows `context.WithTimeout`, simple exponential backoff (3 retries), and `base64.StdEncoding.DecodeString` for resume cursor. Kept the defaults small for docs readability and added a production note.
Noah R.: Lint/formatting: I will run black/prettier after merge if there are small style issues in code blocks.
